candidates.name: Nolan Southerland
candidates.title: Film Editor
candidates.issues: Public housing, rent control, ICE out, police budget
candidates.summary: DSA-LA priority campaign with Mike Van Gorder. Named policies include rent control, tenant protections, public housing, accessible transit, reevaluating police budget and practices, raising the minimum wage, and keeping ICE and Flock out of Burbank.

candidates.name: Mike Van Gorder
candidates.title: Housing Policy Analyst
candidates.issues: Tenant power, housing supply, anti-ICE, labor
candidates.summary: State housing-policy specialist, Planning Commissioner, Glendale Tenants Union founder, union member, and DSA-aligned. Campaign: housing crisis, worker power, public schools, stand up to ICE. 2024: 8,843 votes (4th of 9).

candidates.name: Nikki Perez
candidates.title: Incumbent council member
candidates.summary: First-term record includes a tenant-protection and rent-control ordinance, 2,000+ housing units, a homeless-solutions center, limits on city resources for federal immigration enforcement, and a community assistance fund. 2026 kickoff at IATSE Local 80. Priorities: working families, civil rights, entertainment jobs, affordable housing, environment.

candidates.name: Eddy Polon
candidates.title: Community Advocate / Screenwriter
candidates.issues: Dedicated BRT, missing-middle housing, no local rent cap
candidates.summary: Transportation Commissioner and Strong Towns Burbank co-founder. Endorsed by the Housing Action Coalition, IATSE Local 33, Americans for Democratic Action, and several Democratic legislators. Publicly backs dedicated-lane BRT and missing-middle housing; argues SB 79 is a planning problem, not a reason to block transit. Mid-August 2026 Reddit comment: against a local rent cap. 2024: 8,485 votes (5th of 9).

candidates.name: Tamala Takahashi
candidates.title: Incumbent council member
candidates.issues: Climate, mental health, renter protections, mobility
candidates.summary: Elected 2022. Platform: sustainability, mental-health first response, mobility for all modes, renter protections, housing “thoughtfully in the right places,” arts, inclusivity. Endorsed by Stonewall Democratic Club, LA League of Conservation Voters, Assemblymember Nick Schultz, and Rep. Laura Friedman.

candidates.name: Samantha Wick
candidates.title: Nonprofit Grant Writer / Planner
candidates.issues: Targeted growth, mixed-flow BRT, public safety
candidates.summary: Planning Commissioner. Supports “smart, targeted housing growth that respects neighborhoods,” not blanket density. Prefers mixed-flow BRT rather than a dedicated lane. Fully staffed police and fire. Tenant protections under state AB 1482 plus vouchers; more homeownership, not just rentals.

candidates.name: JT Parr
candidates.title: Comedian
candidates.summary: No 2026 campaign website found. 2024 Burbank Leader interview: increase housing options and ownership, do not forget month-to-month renters, reduce street speeds from 35 to 25 mph. Instagram @jtparr14 is the public channel. Placement uses the 2024 record.

candidates.name: Robbie Brody
candidates.title: Lawyer / Administrative Law Judge
candidates.issues: Neighborhood character, no dedicated BRT, public safety, Flock
candidates.summary: 27-year Burbank resident; lawyer and administrative law judge; Parks, Recreation and Community Services Board through 2029. Site: preserve Rancho, Magnolia Park, and hillside character while supporting sensible housing families can afford; police and fire should have what they need; small business and parks. Message to this guide: a dedicated bus lane is the wrong solution for Burbank; Flock cameras lack due process. Campaign: chaired three boards; current Parks & Rec chair.

candidates.name: Jonathan Ontiveros
candidates.title: Civil Engineering Professional
candidates.summary: No campaign website or Burbank issue platform found. LA County Public Works engineer, CAPE public-employee union board member, and ASCE Metro LA president. LinkedIn also describes him as entrepreneur and investor. Placement near the origin is a low-confidence guess until a city platform appears.

candidates.name: Hovanes Tonoyan
candidates.title: Cyber Security Professional
candidates.summary: 2024 campaign: turn Burbank into a “mecca of entrepreneurship,” keep tax dollars in residents’ pockets, treat every resident as CEO of their own life. 2026 site is live but thin; 2024 forums remain the best record. 5,670 votes in 2024 (6th of 9).

candidates.name: Chris Yoosefi
candidates.title: Small Business Owner
candidates.issues: Rent cap with partnership, mixed-flow BRT, local housing control, public safety
candidates.summary: Navy veteran and small-business owner. Site: cut waste and red tape, revive downtown, “preserve Burbank’s charm,” residents first rather than outside developers. Reddit (YoosefiServes): yes to a local rent cap with discussion and partnership; no dedicated BRT on Olive, mixed-flow OK, prefers another location; more housing without SB 79; not a fan of ICE or Flock; police yes. Will direct police not to assist ICE and will not spend tax dollars fighting the federal government.

candidates.name: David Donahue
candidates.title: Small Business Owner
candidates.summary: Campaign site: davidforburbank.com. President of Vision Burbank and the Burbank Fair Housing PAC. Opposes local rent caps and a rent registry; prefers state AB 1482 plus subsidies. Supports ADU / manufactured-housing supply. Mixed-flow BRT, not dedicated lanes. Construction and development background. Fair Housing PAC posted his 2026 questionnaire on Facebook.

candidates.name: Jackie Waltman
candidates.title: Retired
candidates.summary: No campaign website found. Civil Service Board; former Landlord-Tenant Commission; 2011 council candidate. Letters and council comment: voters already rejected rent control; dedicated BRT and SB 79 are misguided. July 2026 letter argued Perez, Anthony, and Takahashi were circumventing those votes and asked for a new citywide vote.

candidates.name: Kimberley Clark
candidates.title: Incumbent
candidates.summary: Elected 2022. Running unopposed. Professional clerk race; no 2026 campaign platform found. Not plotted on the council issue grid.

candidates.name: Krystle Palmer
candidates.title: Incumbent
candidates.summary: Appointed 2019, elected 2020 and 2022. Running unopposed. Prior campaigns stressed safeguarding taxpayer dollars. No 2026 campaign site found. Not plotted on the council issue grid.

candidates.name: Paul Gerard
candidates.title: College Professor / Parent
candidates.issues: Transparency, fiscal stability, enrollment, students first
candidates.summary: USC animation professor; former Disney, Hasbro, and Warner Bros. executive. Site: Brown Act / transparency, fiscal stability, declining enrollment, and student-first representation. Contact: gerardforbusd@protonmail.com.

candidates.name: Dennis M. Connor
candidates.title: Retired Technical Writer
candidates.summary: Certified candidate. Ballot designation: Retired Technical Writer. Filed August 6, 2026. No website, interview, email, or public comment located yet.

candidates.name: Rosemary T. Morrison
candidates.title: Mother / Teacher / Student
candidates.summary: No 2026 campaign website found. Former Board of Library Trustees (term ended 2024). BUSD parent who in November 2020 backed DEI committee work and asked that core English novels be updated because of harm to Black children. Adjunct environmental-science faculty. Historical comments only — not a current platform.

candidates.name: Evren Ozbey
candidates.title: Candidate
candidates.summary: Certified candidate. County list: (818) 210-6059, evrenozbey17@gmail.com. Filed July 2026 with no ballot designation. No website or interviews found yet.

candidates.name: George Saikali
candidates.title: YMCA CEO
candidates.summary: Unopposed; will be seated after November 3. 41-year YMCA executive; Burbank resident since 1997. Site priorities: classrooms first, financial oversight after LACOE’s “Lack of Going Concern” designation, communication, teachers and staff, multiple student pathways.
